content:
Nuevo Laredo's municipal government says it has applied approximately 19 fines for illegal dumping during the current administration, as part of inspection and surveillance operations to detect and address clandestine dump sites across the city, according to CML Noticias.

Tania Taboada Blanco, head of the Coordinación General de Gestión Ambiental, said the Inspection and Surveillance area handles citizen complaints, carries out patrols, and verifies lots where trash and debris are reported accumulating in public or private spaces.

Reports come in through social media and the 072 line, and staff follow up on each case to identify the location and determine what action is needed, according to the report. When inspectors find a clandestine dump site, they gather evidence and draw a sketch of the site, which is turned over to the legal area to establish whether the land is municipal or private property.

Sanctions are applied under article 331, fraction III, of the applicable regulation, which covers fines for depositing waste on built and unbuilt lots. For private land, the city requests information from the Catastro office to identify owners and notify them so they take responsibility for keeping the space clean; if the instructions are not followed, the procedure continues and the established sanctions can be applied. For municipal land, Gestión Ambiental coordinates cleanup with the Secretaría de Servicios Públicos Primarios.

Taboada Blanco said citizen collaboration is fundamental to locating these sites and keeping them from becoming infection hotspots that pose a public health risk. Residents can report irregular dumping through the 072 telephone line, the 072.mx portal, the Coordinación General de Gestión Ambiental's social media accounts, its offices at Arteaga 3900 in the Centro sector, or by telephone at 867 714 7973.

The municipal government reiterated its call for residents not to throw trash in vacant lots and public spaces, and to report the practice to help keep the city clean and protect families' health.

Sources:

  • CML Noticias, "Aplican 19 multas por tiraderos clandestinos en Nuevo Laredo," October 30, 2026

title: Nuevo Laredo has fined illegal dumping about 19 times — and officials say reports from residents are how they find the sites
